newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - May 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - May 6.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on May 6:
NEW YORK - The stock market soared to a record high in a broad-based rally that surprised skeptics who were predicting a sustained downturn.
JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - A jury found R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Corp RJR.N was not responsible for the lung cancer death of a longtime customer.

TRENTON, NEW JERSEY - Almost three years after the rape and murder of 7-year-old Megan Kanka triggered a national movement to notify communities of sex offenders in their midst, testimony began in the trial of her accused killer, a twice-convicted pedophile who lived across the street.
KINSHASA, ZAIRE - Zairian rebel leader Laurent Kabila said his forces could be in the capital city in the next "two or three days" and were already within 35 miles of Kinshasa's airport.
WASHINGTON - The issue of race emerged in the trial of a second African-American drill sergeant accused of raping an Army trainee at Aberdeen Proving Ground.
FORT DAVIS, TEXAS - One of two Republic of Texas separatists who fled into the mountains after refusing to surrender along with his comrades Saturday died in a gun battle with state police on Monday.
